subject: Partner evidence interop protocol and transfer checklist
messages:
From: Amy Lee <amy@redline-sec.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: redline-sec-support@redline-sec.com
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partner evidence transfer: formats and delivery options

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. As we prepare to onboard Redline Security as a pen-test partner for the upcoming SOC2 cycle, we want to confirm how Redwood prefers to receive evidence artifacts (logs, screenshots, test manifests). Our engineering team can output an "evidence bundle" in a few formats: zipped S3 archives (presigned URLs), SFTP drop, or an API-based upload that accepts multipart/form-data.

Quick clarifying questions:
- Do you require a manifest CSV/JSON describing each artifact (recommended)?
- Are short-lived presigned S3 URLs acceptable, or do you prefer SFTP with per-client accounts?
- Is server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or customer-managed KMS) required for the transfer?

We can attach a template manifest and a proposed scoping checklist — attaching the manifest template for reference.

Example attachment: evidence_requirements.xlsx (stub)

If you can share the internal retention and access audit expectations, we can map our delivery to your audit log needs.

Best,
Amy
Senior Engagement Manager
Redline Security

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy@redline-sec.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner evidence transfer: formats and delivery options

Amy — thanks for the template, and great questions. High level answers so we can pick a concrete flow:

- Manifest: yes, we require a manifest file (CSV or JSON) that contains artifact id, type, creation timestamp, sha256, and associated test ticket ID.
- Transfer method: presigned S3 URLs are preferred for bulk artifacts because they integrate with our ingestion pipelines, but we can support SFTP for partners that require it.
- Encryption: customer-managed KMS is preferred for anything that includes production data. SSE-S3 is acceptable for non-prod artifacts.

Operational constraints and asks:
- Presigned URLs must be single-use and expire in <= 1 hour.
- Each bundle should include an audit manifest and a small summary doc (one page) describing the scope of the test, CVE references, and any special handling notes.
- We will need a signed transfer SLA (we can send a DocuSign) and an onboarding checklist that maps to our evidence retention policy (90 days hot, 365 archive).

Cc'ing Vanessa and Sergio to confirm procurement/privacy and to help with the SLA. I'll follow up with the onboarding play we prefer and a proposed schedule for a dry-run transfer.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Partner Programs — Redwood Inference

From: Amy Lee <amy@redline-sec.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Redline Security Support <redline-sec-support@redline-sec.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner evidence transfer: formats and delivery options

Great — that all sounds doable. A few follow-ups from our side:

- We'll produce both CSV and JSON manifests; we'll add sha256 and ticket links.
- For presigned S3 there are two options on our side: generate presigned URLs ourselves and hand them to you (short-lived), or push to an S3 bucket you control where we are provisioned write access. Which do you prefer?
- KMS: we can support SSE-C or a customer-managed KMS key if you provide an ARN and policies.

I've attached a short attachment with our standard evidence scoping template. Also flagging that our legal counsel likes to see a one-page transfer SLA that includes maximum retention, deletion confirmation, and audit log delivery frequency.

Attachment: evidence_requirements.xlsx (uploaded)

If you want to test an end-to-end flow tomorrow afternoon, we can stand up a small sample payload and run the transfer.

Best,
Amy

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T12:01:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Partner evidence transfer: formats and delivery options

Marcus — forwarding the Redline thread. TL;DR: they can do presigned URLs or SFTP. We prefer presigned S3 to feed our ingestion pipeline but need single-use, short TTL, and KMS support. Can your team: 

- Confirm if our ingestion pipeline can accept presigned uploads from external partners (we currently accept presigned GET/PUT links for uploads from vendor tools).
- Outline the temporary IAM policy we would attach to generated presigned URLs (least privilege).
- Confirm how we will capture an immutable audit trail for each artifact (object metadata + CloudTrail events + ingestion logs).

Notes from me: retention mapping should be: 90 days hot, 365 days cold archive behind EKM; deletion confirmation posted back to partner and saved in the audit manifest.

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 11:24 AM Amy Lee <amy@redline-sec.com> wrote:
> Great — that all sounds doable...

Appreciate quick take here as Redline is requesting a dry-run today.

— Sofia

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy@redline-sec.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T16:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner evidence transfer: formats and delivery options

Amy — thanks for your flexibility. Quick summary and proposed next steps (action items below):

Summary decision:
- Transfer method: presigned S3 PUT URLs, single-use, TTL=60 minutes. Redwood will provide an ingestion endpoint that validates manifest and checks SHA256 before promoting artifacts to long-term storage.
- Encryption: customer-managed KMS for any production-scoped artifacts; SSE-S3 for non-prod. Please provide KMS ARNs when you send the first bundle.
- Manifest: CSV schema accepted; include artifact_id, filename, size_bytes, sha256, timestamp_utc, test_ticket_id, retention_class.

Action items:
1) Redwood (Sofia / Marcus): share interop spec and short onboarding checklist (attached: interop_spec_v1.pdf).
2) Redline (Amy): confirm whether you will generate presigned URLs on your side or allow Redwood to provision an upload bucket and grant write permissions for the dry-run.
3) Legal / Procurement (Vanessa / Sergio): review and sign the one-page transfer SLA (we will send DocuSign link).
4) Dry-run: Target window — 2027-04-29 14:00-15:00 PT. Please confirm availability.

Attachments in this message: interop_spec_v1.pdf (stub), evidence_manifest.csv (sample), sftp_instructions.txt (for fallback).

If this looks good, we'll send the DocuSign SLA and a Confluence onboarding checklist link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/GRC/partner-evidence-interop

Thanks again — looking forward to the dry-run.

Sofia Ivanova
Partner Programs — Redwood Inference
